title: Private Deploy: Interop & Upgrade Acceptance Criteria for Air-gapped and VPC Environments
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket captures product requirements and formal acceptance criteria for Private (VPC and air-gapped) deployments with a focus on networking constraints, upgradeability, and operational interoperability. Goal is to produce a checklist that engineering and SRE teams can use to validate customer installations and to gate releases for private customers.

Background: Several enterprise prospects require a Private offering that can be deployed into restricted network zones (strict egress, NAT-limited subnets, no internet access) and that supports in-place upgrades with clear rollback semantics. Previous notes (PM-482 and PM-731) defined high-level constraints; this ticket turns those into explicit, testable acceptance criteria and runbook items.

Scope: In-scope: network connectivity patterns, allowed outbound flows, upgrade/rollback flow for control plane + runtime, local package distribution (airgap), verification steps, monitoring/telemetry fallbacks, KMS integrations. Out-of-scope: UI redesigns in Console, Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies (handled separately), and full air-gapped CI workflows.

Goals:
- Provide clear, minimal network requirements for VPC and air-gapped installs.
- Define upgrade acceptance criteria (preflight checks, staged rollout, rollback).
- Produce a verification checklist for field engineers and SREs to validate installations.
- Capture trade-offs for telemetry and optional diagnostic upload when air-gapped.

Non-goals:
- Replace the full on-prem packaging system (this ticket requires the existing installer artifacts produced by ENG).
- Create new KMS products; we will document integration points for existing KMS/HSM solutions.

Networking requirements (high level):
- VPC mode: control plane communicates to customer VPC via customer-provided peering or Transit Gateway. Minimum outbound: allow HTTPS (443) to specific Redwood control-plane endpoints when customer opts-in; otherwise use private link (must work without public egress).
- Air-gapped mode: no outbound network access. All artifacts must be provided via signed, downloadable bundles (tar.gz) and a manifest file with SHA256 and signing key fingerprint.
- DNS: provide option for customers to use internal DNS-only names; installer must support overriding DNS and using /etc/hosts or a Kubernetes configmap equivalent.
- NAT/Proxy: installer must support HTTP proxy with basic auth and TLS inspection opt-out.
- Ports: clearly enumerate runtime and control-plane ports required for intra-cluster communication and for optional diagnostics.

Upgrade and rollback requirements:
- Preflight checks: node health, disk usage, KV cache snapshot consistency, current model kernel compatibility matrix. Preflight must fail with actionable errors and remediation hints.
- Staged rollout: upgrades must be able to operate as canary (10% of nodes), progressive (25/50/100), or full. The default progressive window must be configurable.
- Backwards compatibility: new runtime must be compatible with pinned model artifacts for at least two minor releases or provide an automated model-compatibility migration plan.
- Atomic rollback: in the event of a failed upgrade step, the system must revert traffic and runtime binaries within a deterministic timeout and surface a post-mortem link.
- Data migration: any on-disk or KV schema migrations must be reversible or checkpointed with a validated restore path documented in the runbook.

Air-gapped distribution constraints:
- Signed bundles: provide a manifest file with SHA256 and GPG or PKCS7 signing. Installer verifies signatures before install/upgrade.
- Offline verification: provide an offline verification tool that validates bundle integrity and compatibility with current cluster state.
- Patch cadence: document a secure patch transfer process for customers who receive updates via secure media (SFTP, removable media).

Telemetry and observability:
- Default: in VPC mode with outbound allowed, telemetry (usage/health) can be streamed to Redwood endpoints with customer consent.
- Air-gapped: telemetry must be disabled by default; provide an opt-in local archive format (compressed JSON) that customers can export for manual upload.
- Required logs and metrics for support: list of minimal logs (api-server, runtime, supervisor) that must be collected locally and a one-click bundle generator for field support.

Security and KMS:
- KMS integrations: support for AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS, and generic HSM via PKCS11. Document key rotation steps and acceptance criteria for key presence during upgrade.
- Secrets handling: secrets must never be sent to Redwood control plane for air-gapped installs. Documentation must include end-to-end flow diagrams.

Acceptance criteria (testable):
acceptance_criteria: Network doc: A single page that lists minimal network flows and ports for VPC and air-gapped installs, with example firewall rules (pass)
Installer preflight: installer halts on missing dependencies and emits clear remediation steps (pass/fail tests with mock environments)
Signed bundles: bundles contain manifest+signature and installer verifies signature prior to install (verified in CI and manual test)
Upgrade staging: canary->progressive->full upgrade simulated in test lab with automated rollback triggered by injected failure (validated)
Rollback atomicity: traffic reverts to previous runtime within configured timeout and no request loss above defined threshold (SLO: <0.1% request loss during rollback)
Telemetry behavior: in air-gapped installs telemetry disabled by default and local support bundle produced on customer command (manual verification)
KMS checks: upgrade will fail if required KMS key not reachable or rotated mid-upgrade; test harness to simulate key errors (pass)
Runbook: a 2-page runbook for upgrade/rollback including commands, expected outputs, and escalation path (reviewed and signed-off)
Signed acceptance: Security review completed and sign-off recorded in Confluence (link in comments)
verification_plan: Testing will use three environments: a fully connected VPC lab, a restrictive VPC lab (egress via proxy only), and an air-gapped lab. Tests include installer signature verification, preflight failures, canary/progressive upgrade simulation with fault injection, and manual KMS failure tests. Field validation checklist to be used by Solutions Engineers for customer acceptance.

notes_and_tradeoffs:
Trade-offs considered: requiring signed bundles and strict preflight increases integration friction but materially reduces upgrade incidents for air-gapped customers. Supporting both GPG and PKCS7 increases maintenance surface area; initial rollout will require GPG and one PKCS11 path for major HSM vendors, with additional formats added as needed. Telemetry fallback for air-gapped customers will be a manual export to respect data sovereignty.

Open questions:
- Do we require customers to run a Redwood-provided offline verifier, or is a spec sufficient? (action: align with ENG on tooling)
- Exact rollback timeout default (proposal: 5 minutes)
- Should we provide a managed private link offering to avoid egress entirely? (sales/infra input needed)
